anomalies.observed: In the 'Water Level Sensor/Switches' block (root sheet), R6 (10k) is wired as a pull-UP on the FLOAT_HIGH net (top terminal to +3V3, bottom terminal to the wire from J1 pin 2 / FLOAT_HIGH), and R9 (10k) is wired as a pull-DOWN on the FLOAT_LOW net (top terminal to the wire from J1 pin 3 / FLOAT_LOW, bottom terminal to GND).
anomalies.expected: Per the specification's SPICE/netlist excerpt, R6 is the 10k pull-UP on FLOAT_LOW and R9 is the 10k pull-DOWN on FLOAT_HIGH (R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k; R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k). The two float-switch bias resistors have been placed on the opposite nets.

evidence.quote: Root sheet, 'Safety Switches': R6 10k between +3V3 and FLOAT_HIGH; R9 10k between FLOAT_LOW and GND (J1 pin2=HIGH, pin3=LOW).
§4.4: "R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO 4.7k".

anomalies.impact: The idle bias of each float net is inverted relative to the switch wiring and to the interlock resistors R2 (FLOAT_LOW -> T1 base) and R11 (FLOAT_HIGH -> T4 base). With FLOAT_LOW held low by R9, T1 stays off and R5 keeps the main-pump MOSFET T2 on, so the low-level pump cutoff interlock never trips; the high-level overflow interlock on the ATO valve is likewise defeated. The board loses its float-switch safety interlocks and the firmware's level readings are inverted.

parsed.summary: Most of the design matches the specification (power train, ADM3260 isolator topology, TMC2209 drivers, ESP32 pin map, DNP sensors), but the float-switch bias resistors R6 and R9 appear to be connected to the opposite nets (R6 pull-up on FLOAT_HIGH, R9 pull-down on FLOAT_LOW) versus the intended R6 pull-up on FLOAT_LOW / R9 pull-down on FLOAT_HIGH, which would defeat the low-level pump cutoff and high-level overflow interlocks.
